content:
incident-bot: PAGE | P1 - Elevated 5xx + timeouts for tenant theta-fin (vc-22) on dedicated pool dp-22 in eu-central-1. Error rate 48% over 4m. Autoscaler spiking, container restarts observed. Paging oncall.

taylor (oncall): acknowledged. pulling container logs and metrics for dp-22/vc-22. any recent deploys?

taylor (oncall): logs show repeated `OOMKilled` in model-worker-0, then failover attempts. KV cache eviction high. sample log:

```
[14:03:12] model-worker-0[pid:1234]: oom-kill event: rss=18.3G, mem_limit=16G
[14:03:15] scheduler: reschedule tenant vc-22 -> fallback pending
```

mira (sre): looks tenant-noisy. Other tenants on dp-22 unaffected until these OOMs. Hypothesis: model pinned to large-llama variant + long production prompts from theta-fin.

kevin (infra): no infra deploys. dp-22 GPU util ~95%. Protected-tenant reservation set to 12% but metrics show sudden per-container memory spike. autoscaler did not add node in time due to burst-style pattern.

taylor (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) divert vc-22 traffic to dp-18 (fallback) 2) reduce vc-22 concurrency 3) if customer has smaller variant pinned, offer to switch. I can trigger route change if infra ok.

kevin (infra): executing route change now:

```
rmctl route set --tenant vc-22 --from dp-22 --to dp-18 --force --reason "mitigate dp-22 OOMs"
```

deploy-bot: rmctl: route update queued by kevin at 1780012361.

kevin (infra): applied. containers rebalanced on dp-18, warming caches.

taylor (oncall): error rate for vc-22 dropped 48% -> 5% within 60s. latency normalizing. marking mitigation effective for user impact.

lia (support): opened customer bridge, pinged theta-fin SRE and account team. They reported "timeouts and incomplete responses" starting ~14:03 CET. Opening post-incident sync.

sam (acct): drafting short customer note to send now. Proposed: 

"Hi, we observed degraded responses for your dedicated pool in eu-central-1 and routed traffic to an alternate dedicated pool to restore service. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a full RCA and remediation plan. -- Sam (Redwood)"

sam (acct): can we confirm whether naming dp-18 is safe to disclose?

mira (sre): dp-18 is fine to name if customer prefers technical detail. Otherwise say "an alternate dedicated pool in eu-central-1".

taylor (oncall): handing incident for RCA to mira; I'm on rotation change in 25m. Key artifacts to collect: `dmesg` OOM traces, model telemetry (seq lengths + input sizes), scheduler decisions, autoscaler logs.

mira (sre): taking over. immediate actions: 1) collect telemetry for vc-22 for 1h before event 2) verify tenant reservation config 3) create RCA doc draft 4) propose concrete remediations.

kevin (infra): early root cause note: protected-tenant reservation was too low for worst-case prompt lengths; autoscaler configured for sustained load, not short noisy spikes. We'll add an autoscaler heuristic to handle sustained OOM pattern detection.

exec-lin: need customer impact summary + whether SLA credit likely. Need one-paragraph for exec update.

mira (sre): impact window: 14:03 - 14:14 CET (11 minutes) where customer saw errors >5%. After route change errors dropped below 0.2% by 14:16. No other tenants reported user-visible errors.

sam (acct): SLA/credit calc: theta-fin committed monthly spend = EUR 95,000. SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime for dedicated pools in enterprise contract. 11 minutes = 0.00765% of month (~0.0000765 fraction). Standard credit calc suggests small partial credit; given dedicated enterprise contract propose goodwill credit = 5% of monthly committed on dedicated service prorated. Flagging finance.

finance-bot: finance: please confirm credit authorization flow. Ticket FIN-998 created for approval.

lia (support): customer replied: thanks for fast action, please include prevention steps + timeline in RCA. They requested an exec-level summary for their CIO. Scheduling postmortem call Wed 09:00 CET.

mira (sre): RCA draft highlights:
- What happened: theta-fin's workload produced unusually long sequences causing memory pressure on model-worker -> OOMKills -> scheduler churn -> elevated 5xx for tenant on dp-22.
- Why it happened: protected-tenant reservation (12%) insufficient for worst-case model memory footprint; autoscaler heuristics did not trigger node add due to bursty pattern; no auto-failover on OOM spikes for protected tenants.
- Immediate mitigation: manual route to dp-18, lowered concurrency for vc-22, warmed caches.
- Remediations: increase protected-tenant reservation to 30% for dedicated pools by config, implement auto-failover when OOMKill > 2 for tenant in 2m, add model-level seq-length guardrails and customer guidance, add chaos test for noisy tenants.

kevin (infra): creating infra tickets now:
- INF-5121: raised protected-tenant reservation default -> owner kevin -> ETA PR by end of sprint
- INF-5122: autoscaler heuristic + OOM-based auto-failover -> owner kevin/mira -> ETA 2 sprints

sam (acct): I'll send the customer initial note and schedule the postmortem call. Draft email below:

"Subject: Incident report and next steps 

Hi team,
We experienced a degradation affecting your dedicated pool in eu-central-1 starting at 14:03 CET. We routed traffic to an alternate dedicated pool and restored service within ~11 minutes. We're assembling a full RCA and remediation plan and would like to review on Wed 09:00 CET. Apologies for the disruption.

Best, Sam (Redwood)"

mira (sre): please include technical contact (mira@redwood.ai) and link to runbook. Add note offering to test smaller model variant or configure a per-tenant concurrency cap.

exec-lin: exec blurb for leadership: "Tenant theta-fin experienced an 11-minute degradation due to tenant-driven OOMs on dp-22; mitigation was manual failover to dp-18; remediation plan includes increasing tenant reservations and implementing OOM-triggered auto-failover; customer offered goodwill credit and postmortem call."

sam (acct): approved to send. sending now.

deploy-bot: outreach email queued by sam to ops@theta-fin at 1780012405.

lia (support): theta-fin replied: request RCA + timeline for remediations and copy of SLA compute for dedicated service. Flagged to finance for credit confirmation.

mira (sre): assigning follow-up tickets and owners:
- ENG-4580: per-tenant seq-length telemetry + alerting -> runtime team
- ENG-4581: auto-failover hook on OOM pattern -> runtime/infra
- ENG-4582: update protected-tenant defaults to 30% -> infra (kevin)

kevin (infra): starting ENG-4582 PR.

taylor (oncall): wrapping up shift; incident mitigated and in hand for RCA. handing off to mira for follow-ups.

mira (sre): closing active mitigation thread. I'll post RCA doc link and exec note when ready. Postmortem call Wed 09:00 CET.

sam (acct): thanks everyone. I'll coordinate the finance/credit discussion and follow up with the customer. :thumbsup:
